newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end mostly up amid export rumors.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end mostly up amid export rumors.

text.p: CBOT soyoil and soymeal futures closed mostly higher on Wednesday, supported by speculation China and Morocco were looking to buy U.S. vegetable oils, floor traders said.

"They've got their shopping carts out," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co, referring to talk China and Morocco were interested in soyoil and palm oil. USDA on Wednesday reported 20,000 tonnes of soyoil sold to an unkown buyer.
Traders had mixed opinions on that news with some suggesting the oil had been sold to China while others contended Morocco was the buyer.

Soybean crush margins increased again which promised to keep weekly crush levels at record highs, traders noted. Margins for November/December closed up 0.15 cent per bushel at 72.63 cents on Wednesday.
USDA's crop report on Tuesday indicated abundant ending soyoil stocks but strong demand and rumblings of poor new crop oil content should tighten supplies, traders said.
"Early crush seems to indicate oil content is not as good as it should be," a floor trader said.
Soyoil closed up 0.09 cent a lb to down 0.02 while soymeal ended up $1.70 to $3.00 with December up $1.80 at $232.50.
Ideas Tuesday's gains were overdone led to some chart-based selling which limited gains, traders said.

On the day, Farmers Commodity Corp was a noted seller of the December soymeal while Smith Barney sold the January. Dean Witter Reynolds, ADM Investor Services and Prudential Securities were said to be buyers.

In soyoil, Cargill Inc was an active buyer of the March, which fed ideas of upcoming export business. Chicago Corp was a noted buyer of the December while Iowa Grain and Refco Inc were sellers, traders said.
Volume in soymeal futures was estimated by the CBOT at 20,000 contracts, compared with 47,977 on Tuesday. Soyoil volume was estimated at 16,000 contracts, against 29,915 the previous day.
